title: Closing a thread releases the pointer, and a decision's scope derives

completion_criteria.text: Closing a thread releases the active-thread pointer, so the next session reports no crash and no stale hold, and a park after a close is not refused for naming the wrong thread.
completion_criteria.check: node --test test/spawn/close.test.ts exits 0 with a case asserting the pointer is absent after close_thread

completion_criteria.text: record_decision given a criterion_id and no scope renders the derived criterion label on the spine instead of an empty one.
completion_criteria.check: node --test test/spawn/decisions.test.ts exits 0 with a case asserting the rendered scope is not empty

completion_criteria.text: A full hand-off pass over the live server leaves no stale pointer and renders every hand-off field, run end to end rather than asserted from source.
completion_criteria.check: open a thread, record, park with landed, resume, close, then confirm list_threads reports no held pointer

completion_criteria.text: The continuity-ledger rule describes what record_decision actually does with an omitted scope: it is stored as given and reported as null, never derived from a criterion ordinal. Both the in-repo copy and the global copy say so.
completion_criteria.check: grep for a derived criterion N promise in docs/rules/continuity-ledger.md and ~/.claude/rules/common/continuity-ledger.md returns no match, and npm test still exits 0 at 818 of 818

spine.active_goal: Two defects found by a live end-to-end pass over the 6.0.0 hand-off path. Closing a thread leaves the active-thread pointer naming it, and a decision recorded with a criterion_id but no scope renders an empty scope label. Both are reproduced and neither is fixed.
spine.next_step: Reproduce finding one first, because it is the one that bites a real session: close a thread, then call park_thread on a different open thread and watch the refusal name the closed thread as the one being worked. The pointer write lives in src/domain/pointer.ts and close_thread does not call the release path park_thread uses. Write the red test in test/spawn/close.test.ts before touching either file.

open_risks.text: A session that closes a thread and then stops leaves a pointer naming a terminal thread, and the next session compares pointer session identity rather than thread status, so it reports a crash for work that finished cleanly.

The empty scope label is cosmetic on the spine but the documented behaviour promises a derived criterion N, so any reader trusting the rule sees a contradiction rather than a bug, and no test asserts either shape today.

key_decisions.title: The empty decision scope is correct; the documentation is what is wrong
close_thread releases the pointer only when it names the thread being closed, and only after the commit
